rationale: c3 had the largest screening gap (0.181) and was the only candidate with no negative family (0.03/0.39/0.12), but alpha 0.06 is only ~0.47x the L22 style gap (0.129). Matching the natural style gap (~1.0x, ~6.7 of the 51.5 state norm) tests whether the effect grows with dose without pushing beyond the reference style difference.

Upper arm (~1.55x style gap) to bracket the dose-response at the most consistent site/gate. It is capped near 1.5x because larger off-manifold shifts at L22 leave few layers to repair agreement, and the strong-prompt baseline already showed that large CEFR pushes cost morphosyntax and naturalness on the blind panel.

c2 had the second-best gap (0.170) and the largest words-per-turn separation in the right direction (A1 4.6 vs B2 5.2), but one family was negative and alpha 0.10 is only ~0.7x the L20 style gap (0.144). Moving to ~1.04x the gap tests whether the push becomes consistent across families; the earlier site leaves more layers to repair grammar.
Upper arm (~1.5x style gap) matching c3's upper arm in relative terms, so both sites are compared at equal fractions of their natural style difference. The cap is the same grammar-risk ceiling.
